correctness.rationale: For a given finite occurrence, adding a sufficiently large prime power to its start preserves every valuation, hence preserves the factor along that progression. In the prime-to-p modulus m this progression reaches every source phase, arbitrarily late. Writing n=p^k m, the k-fold morphism has a fixed prefix and one final variable position per source block. A length-n slice at any fixed offset retains exactly m such positions; an overhanging next-block prefix is fixed. They recover the m source letters, and coprime recurrence realizes all of them at the required source starts. For ordinary factors at length at least 2p, exposure of two consecutive source letters prevents the all-zero output, and a nonzero position gives the unique residue of the starting offset. Counting the exposures gives the recurrence; below 2p only the all-zero factor overlaps between offsets. The aperiodicity argument and Morse–Hedlund bound then certify the claimed contrasting regimes. The repaired attribution to Sell was independently verified by specializing his complexity formula and checking both the affine intervals and radix scaling. The proofs and parameters of the phase theorem remain unchanged.
residual_risks: Bounded checks do not prove the universal spectrum, which follows from the bijection. No extension to composite bases is asserted.

value.rationale: For nonoverlapping observations, an unknown grid origin is a natural nuisance parameter. The repaired theorem gives an exact factor-level correspondence uniformly in every start phase and certifies a sharp contrast between prime-power and coprime lengths. Neither an unrestricted complexity count nor a result at one origin establishes this stability. The proof identifies when a shifted block carries exactly the m free letters, so the result is useful beyond a numerical recurrence for P.
